title: Pointwise representability assembles into a coherent infinity adjunction
statement: Use infinity categories, mapping spaces and coherent functors as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and small mapping spaces. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor; no presentability or completeness is assumed. It has a right adjoint if and only if for each $d\in\mathcal D$ the presheaf $c\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(c),d)$ is representable, that is, naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,r_d)$ for some $r_d\in\mathcal C$. Dually a functor $i:\mathcal E\to\mathcal C$ has a left adjoint if and only if for each $c\in\mathcal C$ the covariant functor $e\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$ is representable by an object of $\mathcal E$. The representing objects assemble to a coherent functor and an equivalence of mapping-space bifunctors; the universal representing maps are its unit or counit. The resulting adjunction has coherent units, counits and triangle identities, including their higher compatibility data.
